9	DDX Agent is a Go library that implements a coding agent runtime — a tool-calling
10	LLM loop with file read/write, shell execution, navigation helpers, and
11	structured I/O. Designed to be embedded in
12	[DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) and other build orchestrators.
13	Prioritizes local model inference via LM Studio and Ollama, with transparent
14	escalation to cloud providers.

26	```

328	func (r *runtime) ResolveCost(providerSystem, resolvedModel string) (Cost, bool) {
329		if r == nil {
330			return Cost{}, false
331		}
332	
333		systemPricing, ok := r.pricing[providerSystem]
334		if !ok {
335			return Cost{}, false
336		}
337	
338		cost, ok := systemPricing[resolvedModel]
339		if !ok {
340			return Cost{}, false
341		}
342	
343		// Require at least a pre-computed amount or per-MTok rates to be meaningful.
344		if cost.Amount == nil && cost.InputPerMTok == 0 && cost.OutputPerMTok == 0 {
345			return Cost{}, false
346		}
347	
348		if cost.Source == "" {
349			cost.Source = "configured"
350		}
351		if cost.Currency == "" {
352			cost.Currency = "USD"
353		}
354		if cost.PricingRef == "" {
355			cost.PricingRef = fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s", providerSystem, resolvedModel)
356		}
357		return cost, true
358	}

1	# CONTRACT-001: OTel GenAI Telemetry Capture Contract
2	
3	**Status:** Draft  
4	**Owner:** DDX Agent maintainers  
5	**Related:** [ADR-001](../adr/ADR-001-observability-surfaces-and-cost-attribution.md), [FEAT-005](../../01-frame/features/FEAT-005-logging-and-cost.md), [SD-001](../solution-designs/SD-001-agent-core.md)
6	
7	## Purpose
8	
9	This contract defines the OpenTelemetry trace and metric surface that a
10	DDX-compatible coding harness should emit so one analytics tool can consume
11	telemetry from multiple harnesses without per-harness schema logic.
12	
13	This is a telemetry contract, not a replay contract.
14	
15	- **Telemetry contract**: standard analytics surface for traces and metrics
16	- **Replay artifact**: harness-specific local transcript or session log
17	
18	For DDX Agent, JSONL session logs remain the replay artifact and this contract
19	defines the analytics surface emitted alongside them.
20	
21	## Scope Boundary
22	
23	This contract covers:
24	- required span taxonomy for agent runs, LLM calls, and tool execution
25	- correlation rules across runs, conversations, turns, and retries
26	- required OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes
27	- required DDX extension attributes for gaps not covered by OTel
28	- cost attribution fields and precedence rules
29	- timing fields and throughput derivation rules
30	- default content-capture policy and opt-in payload rules
31	- minimum metric emission rules for analytics consumers
32	
33	This contract does **not** define:
34	- local replay file formats such as JSONL transcripts
35	- collector topology, exporters, or backend storage products
36	- project-specific dashboards
37	- provider SDK internals
38	- budget policy or runtime throttling behavior
39	
40	## Conformance Goal
41	
42	A harness conforms to this contract when another team can implement analytics
43	for that harness and compare it with other conforming harnesses without
44	requiring harness-specific schema guesses.
45	
46	## Required Span Taxonomy
47	
48	### 1. Root run span
49	
50	Every bounded harness run emits one root span representing the run itself.
51	
52	- **Span name**: `invoke_agent <harness-name>`
53	- **Required operation**: `gen_ai.operation.name=invoke_agent`
54	- **Required meaning**: one top-level harness run or autonomous sub-run
55	
56	This span is the rollup parent for all LLM and tool spans emitted by that run.
57	
58	### 2. LLM call spans
59	
60	Every outbound provider call attempt emits one child span.
61	
62	- **Span name**: `chat <request-model>`
63	- **Required operation**: `gen_ai.operation.name=chat`
64	- **Required meaning**: one actual provider/gateway request attempt
65	
66	Retries are separate spans, not hidden inside one aggregated span.
67	
68	### 3. Tool execution spans
69	
70	Every tool execution requested by the model emits one child span.
71	
72	- **Span name**: `execute_tool <tool-name>`
73	- **Required operation**: `gen_ai.operation.name=execute_tool`
74	- **Required meaning**: one tool execution attempt
75	
76	### 4. Optional sub-spans
77	
78	Harnesses MAY emit additional internal spans for provider translation,
79	streaming assembly, sandbox startup, or transport details, but those spans are
80	not part of the required cross-harness analytics contract.
81	
82	## Span Relationships
83	
84	### Trace boundary
85	
86	- One top-level harness run SHOULD produce one trace.
87	- All required spans for that run MUST share the same trace ID.
88	- A child autonomous worker or subagent MAY use a new trace if it is an
89	  independent run, but it MUST preserve conversation linkage using the fields
90	  in this contract.
91	
92	### Parent-child rules
93	
94	- The root `invoke_agent` span is the direct or indirect parent of every
95	  `chat` and `execute_tool` span in the run.
96	- A `chat` span and a following `execute_tool` span MAY be siblings under the
97	  root span or the tool span MAY be nested under an agent/framework span, but
98	  the harness MUST preserve the logical turn linkage via attributes.
99	- Analytics consumers MUST rely on the required identity fields below, not
100	  parentage alone, to correlate turns and retries.
101	
102	## Identity and Correlation Contract
103	
104	### Required DDX identity fields
105	
106	These attributes are required on the root span and SHOULD be copied to all
107	required child spans unless stated otherwise.
108	
109	| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Meaning |
110	|---|---|---|---|
111	| `ddx.harness.name` | string | Required | Logical harness name such as `ddx-agent`, `claude-code`, `codex-cli` |
112	| `ddx.harness.version` | string | Recommended | Harness version or build identifier |
113	| `ddx.session.id` | string | Required | Run-local session identifier for the current harness run |
114	| `ddx.parent.session.id` | string | Optional | Parent run/session when this run continues or forks from another run |
115	| `ddx.turn.index` | int | Required on `chat` and `execute_tool` | Logical turn number within the run, starting at `1` |
116	| `ddx.attempt.index` | int | Required on `chat` | Attempt number within the logical turn, starting at `1` |
117	| `ddx.tool.execution.index` | int | Required on `execute_tool` | 1-based position of the tool execution within the logical turn |
118	
119	### Conversation identity
120	
121	- `gen_ai.conversation.id` SHOULD be populated whenever the harness has stable
122	  conversation/session continuity beyond a single run.
123	- If the harness has no broader conversation concept, it SHOULD set
124	  `gen_ai.conversation.id = ddx.session.id`.
125	- A resumed session, carried-forward history run, or subagent branch MUST NOT
126	  invent a new unrelated conversation ID if the broader conversation is the
127	  same.
128	
129	### Agent identity
130	
131	The root span SHOULD also populate:
132	
133	- `gen_ai.agent.name` when the harness exposes a stable agent identity
134	- `gen_ai.agent.version` when available
135	- `gen_ai.agent.id` only when the underlying system exposes one
136	
137	## Provider and Model Identity
138	
139	### Standard OTel fields
140	
141	Every `chat` span MUST populate, when available:
142	
143	- `gen_ai.provider.name`
144	- `gen_ai.request.model`
145	- `gen_ai.response.model`
146	- `server.address`
147	- `server.port`
148	
149	### Provider identity rules
150	
151	- `gen_ai.provider.name` MUST follow the OTel provider naming model and reflect
152	  the instrumentation's best knowledge of the provider family or API surface.
153	- `gen_ai.provider.name` is not required to equal the real billing/runtime
154	  system.
155	
156	### DDX runtime identity extension
157	
158	Every `chat` span MUST populate:
159	
160	| Attribute | Type | Meaning |
161	|---|---|---|
162	| `ddx.provider.system` | string | Actual execution or billing system such as `openai`, `openrouter`, `anthropic`, `lmstudio`, `ollama`, `bragi`, `vidar`, `grendel` |
163	| `ddx.provider.route` | string | Optional routing label or preset used to choose the provider/model |
164	| `ddx.provider.model_resolved` | string | Optional fully resolved routed model identifier if it differs from request alias |
165	
166	The combination of `gen_ai.provider.name`, `ddx.provider.system`,
167	`gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.model`, and `server.address` is the
168	minimum analytics identity surface for comparing providers across harnesses.
169	
170	## Required OTel GenAI Usage Fields
171	
172	Every successful or partially successful `chat` span MUST populate token usage
173	reported by the provider when those values are available:
174	
175	- `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`
176	- `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`
177	- `gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens`
178	- `gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens`
179	
180	If the provider does not expose a value, the attribute MUST be omitted rather
181	than guessed.
182	
183	## Cost Attribution Contract
184	
185	### Cost precedence
186	
187	Cost attribution follows this precedence order:
188	
189	1. provider-reported billed cost
190	2. gateway-reported billed cost
191	3. explicit configured pricing for the exact `ddx.provider.system` and resolved
192	   model
193	4. unknown cost
194	
195	Generic stale pricing tables MUST NOT be used as a fallback.
196	
197	### Cost fields
198	
199	Every `chat` span MUST populate:
200	
201	| Attribute | Type | Requirement | Meaning |
202	|---|---|---|---|
203	| `ddx.cost.source` | string enum | Required | `provider_reported`, `gateway_reported`, `configured`, or `unknown` |
204	| `ddx.cost.currency` | string | Required when amount is known | ISO 4217 currency code, currently expected to be `USD` |
205	| `ddx.cost.amount` | double | Required when amount is known | Total billed or configured amount for the span |
206	
207	Optional detailed cost fields:
208	
209	- `ddx.cost.input_amount`
210	- `ddx.cost.output_amount`
211	- `ddx.cost.cache_read_amount`
212	- `ddx.cost.cache_write_amount`
213	- `ddx.cost.reasoning_amount`
214	- `ddx.cost.pricing_ref`
215	- `ddx.cost.raw`
216	
217	If `ddx.cost.source=unknown`, `ddx.cost.amount` MUST be omitted.
218	
219	### Root-span cost rollup
220	
221	The root `invoke_agent` span SHOULD populate the same cost fields as a session
222	rollup only when every contributing `chat` span has known cost.
223	
224	If every contributing `chat` span has known cost but the provenance differs
225	across turns, the root span MUST still preserve `ddx.cost.amount` as the sum of
226	the known child costs. In that mixed-provenance case the root span MUST NOT
227	invent a synthetic `ddx.cost.source` or `ddx.cost.pricing_ref`; those fields
228	MUST be omitted unless the rollup can be represented by a single, coherent
229	provenance shape. `ddx.cost.currency` MAY be emitted only when it is unambiguous
230	for the entire rollup.
231	
232	If any contributing `chat` span has unknown cost:
233	
234	- root `ddx.cost.source` MUST be `unknown`
235	- root `ddx.cost.amount` MUST be omitted
236	- analytics SHOULD roll up known and unknown child counts separately
237	
238	## Timing Contract
239	
240	### Base timing
241	
242	Span start and end timestamps are authoritative for:
243	
244	- request start time
245	- request completion time
246	- total span duration
247	
248	Harnesses MUST NOT duplicate these timestamps in custom attributes.
249	
250	### DDX timing extensions
251	
252	Custom timing attributes MAY be added on `chat` spans when exposed by the
253	provider or gateway:
254	
255	| Attribute | Type | Unit | Meaning |
256	|---|---|---|---|
257	| `ddx.timing.first_token_ms` | double | ms | Milliseconds from span start to first streamed token |
258	| `ddx.timing.queue_ms` | double | ms | Time spent queued before provider processing |
259	| `ddx.timing.prefill_ms` | double | ms | Prompt/prefill processing duration excluding generation |
260	| `ddx.timing.generation_ms` | double | ms | Output generation window |
261	| `ddx.timing.cache_read_ms` | double | ms | Cache read processing window |
262	| `ddx.timing.cache_write_ms` | double | ms | Cache write processing window |
263	
264	If the provider does not expose a timing window, the attribute MUST be omitted.
265	
266	## Throughput Derivation Rules
267	
268	Throughput is an analytics computation over traces. Harnesses MAY emit derived
269	metrics, but if they do, they MUST use these formulas.
270	
271	### Output throughput
272	
273	`output_tok_per_s` is defined as:
274	
275	1. `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens / (ddx.timing.generation_ms / 1000)` when
276	   `ddx.timing.generation_ms` exists and is greater than zero
277	2. otherwise, if `ddx.timing.first_token_ms` exists,  
278	   `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens / ((span_duration_ms - ddx.timing.first_token_ms) / 1000)`
279	3. otherwise, not available
280	
281	### Cached input throughput
282	
283	`cached_tok_per_s` is defined as:
284	
285	`gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens / (ddx.timing.cache_read_ms / 1000)`
286	
287	only when both values exist and `ddx.timing.cache_read_ms > 0`.
288	
289	### Non-cached input throughput
290	
291	`input_tok_per_s` is defined as:
292	
293	`(gen_ai.usage.input_tokens - gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens) / (ddx.timing.prefill_ms / 1000)`
294	
295	only when:
296	
297	- `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` exists
298	- `ddx.timing.prefill_ms` exists and is greater than zero
299	
300	If cache-read tokens are absent, analytics MAY assume zero cache-read tokens
301	for this formula only when the provider exposes `prefill_ms` and no cache-read
302	field at all.
303	
304	No other throughput formula is conformant.
305	
306	## Tool Execution Contract
307	
308	Every `execute_tool` span MUST populate:
309	
310	- `gen_ai.tool.name`
311	- `gen_ai.tool.type`
312	- `gen_ai.tool.call.id` when the model or harness provides a stable call ID
313	- `ddx.turn.index`
314	- `ddx.tool.execution.index`
315	
316	Optional fields:
317	
318	- `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`
319	- `gen_ai.tool.call.result`
320	
321	### Tool success and failure
322	
323	- Success MUST follow standard OTel error semantics: span status unset, no
324	  `error.type`
325	- Failure MUST set span status to `Error` and populate `error.type`
326	
327	If the tool returns a structured failure that the harness treats as a failed
328	execution, the span MUST still be marked as an error.
329	
330	## Error and Retry Contract
331	
332	### Standard error handling
333	
334	All spans in this contract MUST follow OTel recording-errors guidance.
335	
336	- On failure, set span status to `Error`
337	- On failure, set `error.type`
338	- `error.type` SHOULD be a low-cardinality identifier
339	
340	### Retry semantics
341	
342	- Each actual provider request retry is a separate `chat` span
343	- All retry spans for the same logical turn MUST share the same
344	  `ddx.turn.index`
345	- Retry spans MUST increment `ddx.attempt.index`
346	- Token usage and known cost belong to the specific attempt span that incurred
347	  them and MUST NOT be collapsed silently into another span
348	
349	## Content Capture Policy
350	
351	### Default policy
352	
353	By default, conforming harnesses SHOULD NOT record full prompt bodies,
354	responses, tool arguments, or tool results on span attributes.
355	
356	This keeps the analytics contract portable and avoids leaking large or
357	sensitive payloads by default.
358	
359	### Opt-in structured capture
360	
361	When a harness is configured to capture content on spans or events, it MUST
362	use the standard OTel fields and schemas:
363	
364	- `gen_ai.system_instructions`
365	- `gen_ai.input.messages`
366	- `gen_ai.output.messages`
367	- `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments`
368	- `gen_ai.tool.call.result`
369	
370	### Externalized content references
371	
372	If a harness stores large content externally, it SHOULD record opaque
373	references using:
374	
375	- `ddx.content.ref.system`
376	- `ddx.content.ref.input`
377	- `ddx.content.ref.output`
378	- `ddx.content.ref.tool.arguments`
379	- `ddx.content.ref.tool.result`
380	
381	Each value SHOULD be an opaque URI or stable handle. Analytics consumers MUST
382	not assume any specific storage backend.
383	
384	## Required Metrics
385	
386	Conforming harnesses SHOULD emit the standard OTel GenAI metrics for each
387	completed `chat` span when their OTel stack supports them:
388	
389	- `gen_ai.client.operation.duration`

2	
3	**Status: ADOPTED.** Use these names in code, packaging, and commits effective immediately.
4	
5	Date: 2026-04-27
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Prior renames (from git history): `luce → lucebox`. Current working name: `agent`.
10	
11	One of the project's stated goals is supporting **testing**, **optimization**, and **one-shot results** — which is also why it has no TUI. The naming exploration was scoped to metaphors that fit that one-shot framing: scientists known for a single decisive experiment, famous sharpshooters, and golfers known for hole-in-one / albatross shots.
12	
13	## Proposed names
14	
15	- **Project / repo / package**: `fizeau`
16	- **CLI binary**: `fiz`
17	
18	## Why Fizeau
19	
20	Hippolyte Fizeau (1849) measured the speed of light using a single rotating toothed wheel and a mirror 8 km away — one precise measurement, one clean answer. The metaphor maps unusually well:
21	
22	- **One shot**: one rotation of the cog → one measurement
23	- **Precision over throughput**: not Monte Carlo, not statistical sampling — a single carefully-instrumented observation
24	- **No interactivity**: the cog spins, the light returns or it doesn't. No TUI in the apparatus.
25	- **Bonus**: the Fizeau–Foucault apparatus is literally a measurement *harness*
26	
27	Predates and is more on-brand than Foucault, who is overloaded philosophically.
28

84	## Rename Boundary

86	The rename is **broad** — every public-facing surface and internal reference is updated:
87	
88	- **Go module path** — `go.mod` module declaration, all `import` paths
89	- **Root package** — package name in `main.go` and any top-level package declarations
90	- **CLI binary** — output binary name, `cmd/` directory structure, `main` package
91	- **Config directories** — `~/.config/fizeau`, `~/.local/share/fizeau`, any XDG paths
92	- **Environment variables** — `FIZEAU_*` prefix (e.g. `FIZEAU_HOME`, `FIZEAU_LOG_LEVEL`)
93	- **Public docs** — README, godoc comments, any markdown under `docs/`
94	- **DDx dependency** — any reference to the project name in `.ddx/` configuration or execution artifacts
95	- **Release / updater** — release asset names, self-update endpoints, version tags

97	## Non-Goals
98	
99	- **Historical evidence rewrites** — git history, old commit messages, and archived research docs are **not** rewritten. The rename is forward-looking only.
100	- **Backward-compat aliases** — no `agent` or `lucebox` shim commands, no legacy config migration.
101	- **Domain registration** — acquiring `fizeau.dev` or `fizeau.io` is out of scope for this rename pass.
102	- **Package registry squatting** — publishing placeholder packages on PyPI/npm to block `fiz` is deferred.
103	
104	## Config/Env Policy
105	
106	- **No compatibility window.** The rename is a hard break. Old config paths (`~/.config/agent`, `~/.config/lucebox`) and old env var prefixes (`AGENT_*`, `LUCEBOX_*`) are **not** read or migrated.
107	- Users must re-create config at `~/.config/fizeau` and set `FIZEAU_*` env vars.
108	- If a user has old config present, `fiz` prints a one-line hint pointing to the new path and exits with a non-zero code.
109	
110	## DDx Dependency
111	
112	- The `.ddx/` directory and its configuration (bead queue, execution metadata, project config) reference the project name. All such references are updated to `fizeau`/`fiz`.
113	- DDx execution artifacts (`.ddx/executions/`) are **not** rewritten — they are historical evidence. New executions after the rename will use the new names.
114	- The `ddx init` command must **not** be re-run; the workspace is already initialized.
115	
116	## Rename Mechanism Decision
117	
118	Use a committed, deterministic script for the module/import-path rewrite. Do
119	not use `gopls`/`gorename` for the module path because the change is a literal
120	repository import rewrite, not a single Go symbol rename. Do not leave the
121	mechanism to local model judgment during FZ-010.
122	
123	FZ-010 must create and commit the script at
124	`scripts/rename-fizeau-module.sh` before applying the rewrite. The required
125	dry-run command is:

127	```bash
128	bash scripts/rename-fizeau-module.sh --dry-run
129	```
130	
131	The script owns only the FZ-010 surface:
132	
133	- `go.mod` module path from `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/agent` to
134	  `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau`

136	  path

138	  hooks or printed follow-up commands
139	
140	Root package declarations, exported Go symbol decisions, and `cmd/` directory
141	moves remain split into their dedicated FZ beads. Those beads may use `git mv`

143	models execute the bead-prescribed mechanics rather than choosing a new policy.
144	
145	## Release/Updater Decision
146

521		outputTokens, ok := attrIntOk(attrs, telemetry.KeyUsageOutput)
522		if !ok || outputTokens <= 0 {
523			return 0, false
524		}
525	
526		if generationMS, ok := attrFloatOk(attrs, telemetry.KeyTimingGenerationMS); ok && generationMS > 0 {
527			return float64(outputTokens) / (generationMS / 1000), true
528		}
529	
530		if firstTokenMS, ok := attrFloatOk(attrs, telemetry.KeyTimingFirstTokenMS); ok && firstTokenMS > 0 {
531			remainingMS := spanDurationMS - firstTokenMS
532			if remainingMS <= 0 {
533				return 0, false
534			}
535			return float64(outputTokens) / (remainingMS / 1000), true
536		}
537	
538		return 0, false
539	}

1	# Project rename — Fizeau / fiz
2	
3	**Status: ADOPTED.** Use these names in code, packaging, and commits effective immediately.
4	
5	Date: 2026-04-27
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Prior renames (from git history): `luce → lucebox`. Current working name: `agent`.
10	
11	One of the project's stated goals is supporting **testing**, **optimization**, and **one-shot results** — which is also why it has no TUI. The naming exploration was scoped to metaphors that fit that one-shot framing: scientists known for a single decisive experiment, famous sharpshooters, and golfers known for hole-in-one / albatross shots.
12	
13	## Proposed names
14	
15	- **Project / repo / package**: `fizeau`
16	- **CLI binary**: `fiz`
17	
18	## Why Fizeau
19	
20	Hippolyte Fizeau (1849) measured the speed of light using a single rotating toothed wheel and a mirror 8 km away — one precise measurement, one clean answer. The metaphor maps unusually well:
21	
22	- **One shot**: one rotation of the cog → one measurement
23	- **Precision over throughput**: not Monte Carlo, not statistical sampling — a single carefully-instrumented observation
24	- **No interactivity**: the cog spins, the light returns or it doesn't. No TUI in the apparatus.
25	- **Bonus**: the Fizeau–Foucault apparatus is literally a measurement *harness*
26	
27	Predates and is more on-brand than Foucault, who is overloaded philosophically.
28	
29	## Availability snapshot (checked 2026-04-27)
30	
31	| Slot | Status |
32	|---|---|
33	| PyPI `fizeau` | Free (404) |
34	| npm `fizeau` | Free (404) |
35	| PyPI `fiz` | Taken but empty/abandoned (no description, no author) |
36	| npm `fiz` | Taken — old fis3 plugin tool, last release 1.4.5, dormant |
37	| GitHub `fizeau` repos | Top hit: `averne/Fizeau` (467★, Nintendo Switch color tool). No AI/dev/agent collisions. |
38	| GitHub `fiz` short name | Some noise: FizzBuzz, `facebook/fizz` (TLS-1.3, different spelling), `fizsh`. No agent/eval tooling. |
39	| `/usr/bin/fiz*`, `/usr/local/bin/fiz*` | Nothing installed |
40	| `fizeau.dev` / `fizeau.io` | DNS doesn't resolve (likely registrable) |
41	| `fiz.dev` | Resolves (likely parked) |
42	
43	## Other names considered
44	
45	Scientists: **eratos** (Eratosthenes — clean, good story), **eddington** (1919 eclipse, mild collision with cycling/astronomy), **cavendish** (heavy collision — Cavendish Lab, banana cultivar), **millikan** (workable, less euphonic).
46	
47	Sharpshooters: **hathcock** (Carlos Hathcock, near-zero collision, slightly grim), **hayha** (Simo Häyhä, darker connotation), **oakley** (killed by sunglasses brand), **deadeye** (generic but clean in AI/dev space).
48	
49	Golf / hole-in-one: **sarazen** (Gene Sarazen's 1935 "shot heard round the world", uncommon), **albatross** (heavy collision), **ace** (no wiggle room).
50	
51	Other one-shot motifs: **ricochet**, **potshot**, **breakshot**.
52	
53	Fizeau won on theme fit + cleanest namespace.
54	
55	## Open risks before adopting
56	
57	1. **Pronunciation split** — English speakers will hit "fih-ZOH" vs "FEE-zoh" vs "FYE-zoh". Pick one and document in README.
58	2. **Dormant `fiz` squatters** — if we ever publish a Python or Node package, distribution name will need to be `fizeau-cli` or similar even if the binary is `fiz` (ripgrep/`rg` pattern).
59	3. **`averne/Fizeau` GitHub overlap** — will share search results until this repo outranks it. Self-correcting, minor.
60	
61	## If adopted
62	
63	Follow the `luce → lucebox` playbook: repo rename, module/import paths, binary name, version bump release commit.
64	
65	## Tagline candidates
66	
67	- *"measure once, cleanly"*
68	- *"one rotation, one number"*
69	- *"the speed-of-light eval harness"*
70	
71	
72	
73	## Target Names
74	
75	| Artifact | Name |
76	|---|---|
77	| Project / repo / package | `fizeau` |
78	| CLI binary | `fiz` |
79	| Go module path | `fizeau` (e.g. `github.com/<org>/fizeau`) |
80	| Root package | `fizeau` |
81	
82	Pronunciation: **FYE-zoh** (rhymes with "size-oh"). Document in README.
83	
84	## Rename Boundary
85	
86	The rename is **broad** — every public-facing surface and internal reference is updated:
87	
88	- **Go module path** — `go.mod` module declaration, all `import` paths
89	- **Root package** — package name in `main.go` and any top-level package declarations
90	- **CLI binary** — output binary name, `cmd/` directory structure, `main` package
91	- **Config directories** — `~/.config/fizeau`, `~/.local/share/fizeau`, any XDG paths
92	- **Environment variables** — `FIZEAU_*` prefix (e.g. `FIZEAU_HOME`, `FIZEAU_LOG_LEVEL`)
93	- **Public docs** — README, godoc comments, any markdown under `docs/`
94	- **DDx dependency** — any reference to the project name in `.ddx/` configuration or execution artifacts
95	- **Release / updater** — release asset names, self-update endpoints, version tags
96	
97	## Non-Goals
98	
99	- **Historical evidence rewrites** — git history, old commit messages, and archived research docs are **not** rewritten. The rename is forward-looking only.
100	- **Backward-compat aliases** — no `agent` or `lucebox` shim commands, no legacy config migration.
101	- **Domain registration** — acquiring `fizeau.dev` or `fizeau.io` is out of scope for this rename pass.
102	- **Package registry squatting** — publishing placeholder packages on PyPI/npm to block `fiz` is deferred.
103	
104	## Config/Env Policy
105	
106	- **No compatibility window.** The rename is a hard break. Old config paths (`~/.config/agent`, `~/.config/lucebox`) and old env var prefixes (`AGENT_*`, `LUCEBOX_*`) are **not** read or migrated.
107	- Users must re-create config at `~/.config/fizeau` and set `FIZEAU_*` env vars.
108	- If a user has old config present, `fiz` prints a one-line hint pointing to the new path and exits with a non-zero code.
109	
110	## DDx Dependency
111	
112	- The `.ddx/` directory and its configuration (bead queue, execution metadata, project config) reference the project name. All such references are updated to `fizeau`/`fiz`.
113	- DDx execution artifacts (`.ddx/executions/`) are **not** rewritten — they are historical evidence. New executions after the rename will use the new names.
114	- The `ddx init` command must **not** be re-run; the workspace is already initialized.
115	
116	## Rename Mechanism Decision
117	
118	Use a committed, deterministic script for the module/import-path rewrite. Do
119	not use `gopls`/`gorename` for the module path because the change is a literal
120	repository import rewrite, not a single Go symbol rename. Do not leave the
121	mechanism to local model judgment during FZ-010.
122	
123	FZ-010 must create and commit the script at
124	`scripts/rename-fizeau-module.sh` before applying the rewrite. The required
125	dry-run command is:
126	
127	```bash
128	bash scripts/rename-fizeau-module.sh --dry-run
129	```
130	
131	The script owns only the FZ-010 surface:
132	
133	- `go.mod` module path from `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/agent` to
134	  `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau`
135	- Go import paths and active non-historical references that name the old module
136	  path
137	- `gofmt`, `go mod tidy`, `go build ./...`, and `go test ./...` verification
138	  hooks or printed follow-up commands
139	
140	Root package declarations, exported Go symbol decisions, and `cmd/` directory
141	moves remain split into their dedicated FZ beads. Those beads may use `git mv`
142	or focused manual edits where their acceptance criteria say so, but local
143	models execute the bead-prescribed mechanics rather than choosing a new policy.
144	
145	## Release/Updater Decision
146	
147	**Release repository**: The canonical release repository after the rename is
148	`DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau`. `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` is treated only as the old
149	location that GitHub may redirect from; release tooling, installer snippets, and
150	self-update code must not rely on that redirect as a supported contract.
151	
152	**Exact choreography**:
153	
154	1. Land the rename change on `master` while still in the old checkout. The
155	   change updates module/import paths, binary names, config/env names, docs,
156	   installer constants, release asset names, and updater constants to
157	   `fizeau`/`fiz`.
158	2. Rename the GitHub repository from `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` to
159	   `DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau` before publishing any renamed release tag. This
160	   ensures the tagged Go module path and release URLs are canonical at the
161	   moment downstream consumers fetch them.
162	3. Create a traceability tag named `rename/fizeau` at the rename commit.
163	4. Create the first pre-release tag and GitHub pre-release as `v1.0.0-rc.1`.
164	   The current binary version is `v0.0.8`, so `v1.0.0` is the next major
165	   without requiring a Go module `/v2` path.
166	5. Publish only new-name assets for the pre-release:
167	   `fizeau-v1.0.0-rc.1-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz` containing a `fiz` binary, plus any
168	   checksums under the `fizeau` name.
169	6. Bump DDx downstream to consume
170	   `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau@v1.0.0-rc.1` and invoke `fiz`. Run the
171	   DDx integration checks there before cutting a final release.
172	7. If DDx exposes a rename defect, fix it in this repository and repeat with
173	   `v1.0.0-rc.2`, `v1.0.0-rc.3`, and so on. DDx must be bumped to the newest
174	   accepted RC before final.
175	8. Create the final `v1.0.0` tag and GitHub release from the exact commit
176	   validated by the accepted RC. Publish the same new-name asset pattern as the
177	   RC with the final version.
178	9. Update DDx from the accepted RC to `github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/fizeau@v1.0.0`
179	   after the final release is live.
180	
181	**Bridge artifacts**: **No.** Do not publish `ddx-agent-*` binaries, tarballs,
182	checksums, aliases, or a final `DocumentDrivenDX/agent` release that points to
183	the renamed project. Do not add an old `ddx-agent update` bridge that downloads
184	`fiz` or rewrites user config. Existing `ddx-agent` installs stop at their last
185	old-name release and users move by installing `fiz` from the renamed repository.
186	
187	**Rationale**: This keeps the rename consistent with the no compatibility
188	window policy above: there is one supported repo, one supported binary name, one
189	config/env namespace, and one update endpoint after the break. The RC gives DDx
190	a real published artifact to validate before the final release without creating
191	a parallel old-name distribution channel that would need its own support and
192	failure handling.

520	func outputTokensPerSecond(attrs []attribute.KeyValue, spanDurationMS float64) (float64, bool) {
521		outputTokens, ok := attrIntOk(attrs, telemetry.KeyUsageOutput)
522		if !ok || outputTokens <= 0 {
523			return 0, false
524		}
525	
526		if generationMS, ok := attrFloatOk(attrs, telemetry.KeyTimingGenerationMS); ok && generationMS > 0 {
527			return float64(outputTokens) / (generationMS / 1000), true
528		}
529	
530		if firstTokenMS, ok := attrFloatOk(attrs, telemetry.KeyTimingFirstTokenMS); ok && firstTokenMS > 0 {
531			remainingMS := spanDurationMS - firstTokenMS
532			if remainingMS <= 0 {
533				return 0, false
534			}
535			return float64(outputTokens) / (remainingMS / 1000), true
536		}
537	
538		return 0, false
539	}

2	
3	**Status:** Draft  
4	**Owner:** DDX Agent maintainers  
5	**Related:** [ADR-001](../adr/ADR-001-observability-surfaces-and-cost-attribution.md), [FEAT-005](../../01-frame/features/FEAT-005-logging-and-cost.md), [SD-001](../solution-designs/SD-001-agent-core.md)
6	
7	## Purpose
8	
9	This contract defines the OpenTelemetry trace and metric surface that a
10	DDX-compatible coding harness should emit so one analytics tool can consume
11	telemetry from multiple harnesses without per-harness schema logic.
12	
13	This is a telemetry contract, not a replay contract.
14	
15	- **Telemetry contract**: standard analytics surface for traces and metrics
16	- **Replay artifact**: harness-specific local transcript or session log
17	
18	For DDX Agent, JSONL session logs remain the replay artifact and this contract
19	defines the analytics surface emitted alongside them.
20	
21	## Scope Boundary
22	
23	This contract covers:
24	- required span taxonomy for agent runs, LLM calls, and tool execution
25	- correlation rules across runs, conversations, turns, and retries
26	- required OpenTelemetry GenAI attributes
27	- required DDX extension attributes for gaps not covered by OTel
28	- cost attribution fields and precedence rules
29	- timing fields and throughput derivation rules
30	- default content-capture policy and opt-in payload rules
31	- minimum metric emission rules for analytics consumers
32	
33	This contract does **not** define:
34	- local replay file formats such as JSONL transcripts
35	- collector topology, exporters, or backend storage products
36	- project-specific dashboards
37	- provider SDK internals
38	- budget policy or runtime throttling behavior
39	
40	## Conformance Goal
41	
42	A harness conforms to this contract when another team can implement analytics
43	for that harness and compare it with other conforming harnesses without
44	requiring harness-specific schema guesses.
45	
46	## Required Span Taxonomy
47	
48	### 1. Root run span
49	
50	Every bounded harness run emits one root span representing the run itself.
